items.question: What is the true nature of the supreme reality described as partless and eternal?
premises: The supreme is free from disease and stain.
items.inference: The supreme reality is pure, undivided, and imperishable.
uncertainties: The exact syntactic role of paraṃ is unclear.
items.plain_english: He is the supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease and stainless.

items.question: Who is the jīva when identified with the supreme haṃsa principle?
premises: The haṃsa is power and individual.
items.inference: The jīva is ultimately the supreme haṃsa composed of power and individuality.
uncertainties: The precise relation between jīva and haṃsa is not fully explicit.
items.plain_english: He is the soul, supreme indeed; he is the haṃsa, power and individual.

items.question: Where is the wind-filled air situated among all beings?
premises: It is situated in all beings.
items.inference: The vital air pervades and is established in every being.
uncertainties: The exact referent of saṃsthitam is not fully explicit.
items.plain_english: The wind-filled air is situated in all beings.

rows.grounds: compound of deha, tyakta, and mātreṇa

items.question: What happens to the jīva when it merely leaves the body?
premises: Upon merely leaving the body, he is called supreme.
items.inference: The jīva becomes identified with Śiva immediately upon leaving the body.
uncertainties: Whether paraṃ modifies Śiva or the state is unclear.
items.plain_english: He, upon merely leaving the body, is called supreme Śiva.

rows.grounds: compound of pāramparya, krama, and āgatam

items.question: How is the teaching that abides in the ear transmitted?
premises: It has come down through tradition.
items.inference: The doctrine is received by hearing and preserved through traditional transmission.
uncertainties: The exact object of śrūyate is not explicit.
items.plain_english: O goddess, what abides in the ear is heard, having come down through tradition.

items.question: What is accomplished by mere knowledge that has been heard?
premises: By this mere knowledge, heard, one attains the result.
items.inference: Mere heard knowledge is sufficient for the stated spiritual attainment.
uncertainties: The exact result attained is not stated in this verse.
items.plain_english: By this mere knowledge, heard, O fair-faced one.
